_about: Machine-readable rule -> source register for the Episode 5 measurement-design checker. Consumed by scripts/check_design.py for citations, and by the Episode 5 pre-slide currency gate to identify which AWS relationships must be re-verified.

S-DATASETMETRIC.title: Amazon Bedrock API Reference - EvaluationDatasetMetricConfig
S-DATASETMETRIC.relationship: metricNames valid values differ depending on whether the job uses a model as judge; metricNames array bounds

S-AUTOEVALCONFIG.title: Amazon Bedrock API Reference - AutomatedEvaluationConfig
S-AUTOEVALCONFIG.relationship: datasetMetricConfigs array bounds; evaluatorModelConfig is an optional member that computes the evaluation metrics

S-PROMPTDATASETS.title: Amazon Bedrock User Guide - Use prompt datasets for model evaluation
S-PROMPTDATASETS.relationship: referenceResponse is required for accuracy and robustness evaluations in a custom prompt dataset; custom dataset prompt limit

S-JUDGEDATASETS.title: Amazon Bedrock User Guide - Create a prompt dataset for a model evaluation job that uses a model as judge
S-JUDGEDATASETS.relationship: referenceResponse is optional for judge jobs; one unique modelIdentifier per job when supplying your own inference responses; dataset prompt limit

R1.condition: When evaluatorModelConfig is absent, every entry in metricNames must be one of the metric names AWS documents as valid for automated model evaluation jobs.

R2.condition: When evaluatorModelConfig is present, every entry in metricNames must be one of the metric names AWS documents as available to model evaluation jobs that use a model as judge.

R3.condition: When a custom prompt dataset is used with Builtin.Accuracy or Builtin.Robustness, every record must carry referenceResponse.

R4.condition: datasetMetricConfigs must contain between 1 and 5 items.

R5.condition: metricNames must contain between 1 and 25 items.

R6.condition: A custom prompt dataset may contain at most 1000 prompts.

R7.condition: When supplying your own inference responses, exactly one unique modelIdentifier may appear, and every record must carry it.

N1.subject: taskType valid values
N1.why_not_enforced: The API reference lists Summarization, Classification, QuestionAndAnswer, Generation and Custom. AWS's own model-as-a-judge examples use taskType 'General', which is not in that list. The evidence contradicts itself, so no taskType value is accepted or rejected here.

N2.subject: built-in dataset name casing
N2.why_not_enforced: AWS documentation shows both Builtin.BOLD and Builtin.Bold for the same dataset. Dataset name spelling is therefore not checked.

N3.subject: task type to dataset pairing
N3.why_not_enforced: AWS documents which datasets are recommended for a task type and which the console offers. It does not document the pairing as a constraint, so it is not enforced as one.

N4.subject: whether the measurement is appropriate to your intent
N4.why_not_enforced: This is a judgement, not a documented constraint. No part of this checker can decide it. A configuration can satisfy every rule above and still measure something other than what you set out to learn.
